props.gloss_en: the mishna: [Torah] scrolls are written in any language
the mishna: tefillin and mezuzot are written only in Ashurit
RSBG: even for scrolls they permitted [another language] only Greek
the baraita: scripture written as targum, targum written as scripture, and Hebrew script do not render the hands impure until one writes it in Ashurit script, on a scroll, in ink
Rava: no difficulty -- the mishna speaks of [another language] in our script, the baraita of [another language] in their script
rather, no difficulty: this [the mishna] is the Rabbis, that [the baraita] is RSBG
rather, no difficulty: here [the mishna] scrolls, there [the baraita] tefillin and mezuzot
tefillin and mezuzot -- what is the reason? because it is written of them 'and they shall be' (Deut 6:6): as they are, so shall they be
rather, no difficulty: here [the baraita] the Megilla, there [the mishna] scrolls
the Megilla -- what is the reason? because it is written of it 'according to their writing and according to their language' (Est 8:9)
Rav Pappa: 'and the king's decree (pitgam) shall be heard' (Est 1:20) -- [the Megilla does contain targum]
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: 'and all the wives shall give honour (yekar) to their husbands' (Est 1:20) -- [the Megilla does contain targum]
Rav Ashi: that baraita is taught of the other books [of scripture]
Rav Ashi: and it is R' Yehuda's
the baraita as Rav Ashi cites it: tefillin and mezuzot are written only in Ashurit, and our Rabbis permitted Greek [for them]
the stam's first emendation: scrolls are written in any language, and our Rabbis permitted Greek
the stam's second emendation: our Rabbis permitted them [scrolls] to be written only in Greek
R' Yehuda: even when our Rabbis permitted Greek, they permitted it only in a Torah scroll
R' Yehuda: and [it was permitted] because of the maaseh of King Ptolemy
King Ptolemy gathered seventy-two elders, put them in seventy-two houses without revealing why, went in to each and said: write for me the Torah of Moses your teacher
the Holy One put counsel in the heart of each one, and all agreed to one understanding
they wrote for him: 'God created in the beginning' (for Gen 1:1, Steinsaltz)
'I shall make man in image and in likeness' (for Gen 1:26, Steinsaltz)
'and He finished on the sixth day and rested on the seventh day' (for Gen 2:2, Steinsaltz)
'male and female He created him' -- and they did not write 'created them' (for Gen 5:2, Steinsaltz)
'come, let me go down and confound their language there' (for Gen 11:7, Steinsaltz)
'and Sarah laughed among her relatives' (for Gen 18:12, Steinsaltz)
'for in their anger they slew an ox and in their will uprooted a trough' (for Gen 49:6, Steinsaltz)
'and Moses took his wife and sons and set them on a carrier of people' (for Ex 4:20, Steinsaltz)
'and the dwelling of the children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt and in other lands was four hundred years' (for Ex 12:40, Steinsaltz)
'and he sent the elect (za'atutei) of the children of Israel' (for Ex 24:5, Steinsaltz)
'and upon the elect of the children of Israel He laid not His hand' (for Ex 24:11, Steinsaltz)
'not one desirable thing (chemed) of theirs have I taken' (for Num 16:15, Steinsaltz)
'which the Lord your God allotted to give light to all the peoples' (for Deut 4:19, Steinsaltz)
'and he went and served other gods, which I did not command [anyone] to serve' (for Deut 17:3, Steinsaltz)
and they wrote for him 'the short-legged beast', and did not write for him 'the hare' (for Lev 11:6, Steinsaltz)
because Ptolemy's wife was named Arnevet, lest he say: the Jews mocked me and put my wife's name in the Torah

answered_by.gloss_en: כאן במגילה, כאן בספרים -- the baraita speaks of the Megilla (= p_kan_bimegillah; its difficulty answered at 9a.7)
כי תניא ההיא בשאר ספרים ורבי יהודה היא -- the baraita speaks of the other books and is R' Yehuda's (= p_ashi_shear_sefarim, p_ashi_ryehuda_hi)

objections.gloss_en: במאי אוקימתא להא? בגופן שלהן -- מאי איריא מקרא שכתבו תרגום ותרגום שכתבו מקרא? אפילו מקרא שכתבו מקרא ותרגום שכתבו תרגום נמי, דהא קתני: עד שיכתבנו אשורית על הספר בדיו! -- in their script even scripture written as scripture would be excluded, so why does the baraita single out the crossings?
אי רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, הא איכא יוונית! -- RSBG permits Greek, but the baraita admits only Ashurit

מאי תרגום שכתבו מקרא איכא? בשלמא תורה — איכא יגר שהדותא, אלא הכא מאי תרגום איכא? -- the Torah contains targum (Gen 31:47), but what targum is there in tefillin and mezuzot for the baraita's 'targum written as scripture'?
מאי תרגום שכתבו מקרא איכא? -- what targum written as scripture is there in the Megilla?

answered_by.gloss_en: וכל הנשים יתנו יקר לבעליהן (Est 1:20) (= p_yekar_targum)

objections.gloss_en: והכתיב והיו! -- tefillin and mezuzot must be as they are written, so 'our Rabbis' cannot have permitted Greek for them
התירו?! מכלל דתנא קמא אסר! -- 'permitted' implies the first clause forbade Greek, yet it says scrolls are written in any language
